input.prompt:
Review the scanned objects' types by eye and write a corrections file. Don't change any other code, don't push or merge.

Data: $S/pr2_scene/assets_mapped.json (440 objects; `label`, `description`, `mobility`, bbox, `mapping`). Run your own API on 8501 (uvicorn --app-dir YOUR worktree, env as before) and viewer on 8524 with `--api-port 8501`, same scene args as 8124, real GPU Chromium args. Stop them when done.

Which objects: every object EXCEPT those labelled pipe, cable or hose whose description agrees they're a pipe, cable or hose. That leaves roughly 200: all "object", appliance, door, pump, valve, sensor, gauge, light fixture, pipe fitting, electrical cabinet, tank, plus movable things (cart, box, bag, ladder, bucket, tool, shelf, chair). The 30 objects with a `mapping` and the door matter most.

How: for each object, put the camera at `GET /api/objects/{id}/view` (scene coords; convert with root.localToWorld, eye 1.6 m above floor, look at the object's centre), or closer if the object is small, and screenshot a crop around its projected box with the frame visible. Combine crops into contact sheets (e.g. 3 x 4, each tile captioned with object_id, current label and the first words of its description), save them under $S/review/, and LOOK at each sheet yourself with the Read tool. Use the description and visible_text as extra evidence. Keep image count reasonable: contact sheets, not one image per object.

Labels to use: the existing vocabulary (pump, motor, valve, sensor, gauge, tank, electrical cabinet, control panel, pipe, pipe fitting, light fixture, door, appliance, cart, box, bag, ladder, bucket, tool, shelf, chair, cable, hose, object), adding "washing machine" or other plain names only when clearly right. Use "object" when you honestly can't tell. Only correct CLEAR mistakes. Note mobility only where it's clearly wrong (a fixed pump marked movable, a loose bucket marked fixed).

Output: commit `scenes/equipment_room.labels.json` on a branch `viktor/label-review`:
{"scene": "equipment_room", "reviewed": "2026-11-07", "method": "...", "fixes": [{"object_id": ..., "center": [x,y,z] (the object's current centre, so a different extraction can't pick it up by mistake), "label": new, "was": old, "mobility": optional, "evidence": "what you saw, under 15 words"}]}
Plus a short markdown summary in the commit message: counts by old to new label, and how many motors, pumps, valves, sensors and transmitters there now are (the Excel pack has 6 pumps, 6 motors, 12 control valves, 3 pressure transmitters and 3 vibration sensors). Commit trailer "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>".

Report: the counts, the file path and commit, the 10 most important fixes (mapped objects and the door first), and anything you couldn't judge.
